title: COMP70050: Deep Learning & Optimization Dynamics
subtitle: Imperial College London — Lecture 4: From Chain Rule to Adaptive Momentum

nodes.label: Multivariable Chain Rule
nodes.summary: Computes derivatives of composite functions along directed computation graphs via Jacobian products.

quiz.question: If z = f(y) and y = g(x), what is dz/dx in matrix form?
quiz.explanation: By the multivariable chain rule, the Jacobian of a composition is the matrix product of individual Jacobians.

nodes.label: Reverse-Mode AutoDiff (Backprop)
nodes.summary: Propagates sensitivity dL/dh backward from scalar loss L in O(1) passes regardless of parameter count.

quiz.question: Why is reverse-mode preferred over forward-mode AD for neural networks?
options: It uses zero memory during forward pass
We have millions of inputs (weights) and 1 scalar output (loss)
quiz.explanation: Reverse-mode computes gradients with respect to all N parameters in a single backward pass when output dimension is 1.

nodes.label: Vanishing & Exploding Gradients
nodes.summary: Repeated multiplication by weight matrices W^L causes gradients to shrink exponentially when singular values σ(W) < 1.

quiz.question: What happens to ∂L/∂h_1 across L layers when the largest singular value σ_max(W) < 0.5?
options: Gradients decay faster than (0.5)^L toward zero
quiz.explanation: Each layer multiplies the backpropagated vector by W^T; when spectral norm < 1, norms shrink exponentially with depth L.

nodes.label: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)
nodes.summary: Updates parameters θ_{t+1} = θ_t - η ∇L_B(θ_t) using mini-batch estimates, introducing isotropic gradient noise.

quiz.question: How does reducing mini-batch size B affect SGD dynamics?
options: Increases stochastic noise covariance, helping escape sharp local minima
quiz.explanation: Smaller batches increase gradient variance Var(g) ∝ 1/B, acting as implicit thermal noise.

nodes.label: Polyak Heavy-Ball Momentum
nodes.summary: Accumulates velocity v_{t+1} = β v_t + ∇L(θ_t) to damp oscillations across high-curvature ravines.

quiz.question: In an ill-conditioned quadratic ravine, what role does the momentum coefficient β play?
options: Cancels opposite-sign gradients across the ravine while accelerating along the valley floor
quiz.explanation: Momentum averages out high-frequency sign flips perpendicular to the valley while compounding consistent descent directions.

nodes.label: Adam Optimizer (Adaptive Moments)
nodes.summary: Combines first-moment momentum (m_t) with per-parameter second-moment RMS scaling (v_t) and bias correction.

quiz.question: Why does Adam divide m_t by (1 - β_1^t) during early steps?
options: Because m_0 is initialized at 0, biasing early estimates toward zero
quiz.explanation: Zero-initialization biases the exponential moving averages toward zero in initial iterations t=1..10.
